scope: On Becoming.LinearBlankets, over Mathlib's reals and matrices, for finitely many coordinates, stated algebraically: a linear drift -B x with noise D, steady covariance S and precision P; the correspondences (the Lyapunov equation as stationarity for B stable, a zero precision entry as conditional independence for a Gaussian, the steady current Q P x times the density, the discrete Lyapunov equation as the synchronous recursion's stationarity where its step matrix has spectral radius below 1, the stochastic time-unrolled blanket under independence of the agent's noise and conditions on the start) are stated, not proved. The Lyapunov equation is the Helmholtz form B = (D - Q) P with Q antisymmetric, its parts unique. Row i of Q P vanishes exactly where row i of Q does; with noise diagonal and positive and no solenoidal flow through i, the drift at i reads j exactly where their precision entry is nonzero; where the drift at i does not read j, their precision entry is nonzero exactly where (Q P) i j does not vanish. With diagonal positive noise and Q vanishing between a set of coordinates and the rest, no coordinate of the set reading j gives a zero precision between the set and j; in the principle's four parts, with internal and active coordinates autonomous (the 2023 paper's footnote 13), sparse coupling gives a zero precision between internal and external coordinates. Under term-by-term sparse coupling (the 2023 paper's eq. 9, with constant Q, noise and Hessian, positive noise and Hessian diagonals) an absent influence has no Hessian and no solenoidal entry, the reverse influence runs only through solenoidal flow to third states, and a state no other state reads reads no other state. Witnesses: a lag relay, sparse both ways as zero drift entries by cancellation, not term by term, with a nonzero precision entry between internal and external coordinates; a steady state circulating through the internal coordinate with the zero entry kept, also by cancellation; a zero entry with the internal drift reading the external coordinate; four coordinates, sparsely coupled term by term, circulating between internal and active coordinates with the zero entries kept. The internal mode reads no external state exactly at the zero block. On Becoming.Blanket: the Euler step of a drift with the principle's sparse coupling is a blanketed law part by part, so runs alike on the sensory coordinates from one internal and active state are alike on the internal and active ones; with additive noise as each coordinate's own input the same holds given one noise course at the internal and active coordinates. Without circulation (B = D P, D and P symmetric) the synchronous scheme's steady precision is P - (h/2) P D P; with D diagonal and positive and the four-part sparse coupling its internal-external entries are zero and its active-external entries are -h/2 times a sum through the sensory coordinates (-h/2 for the four-coordinate witness's precision with noise one). With circulation the four-coordinate witness's synchronous steady precision at h = 1/10 has internal-external entry -27800/984581, while the coupling form holds on its runs. A three-coordinate chain, sparsely coupled under no assignment to the four parts with its ends internal and external, has entry -h/2 between its ends.
